doc.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023

title: Family music: father's Italian feast band
summary: His father, uncles all musicians; he began on drums at eight in his father's Italian feast band and ended up on trumpet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: It is nice. I’ve always wanted to be a quintessential something. But it’s nice that he pointed that out. I’m curious about what kind of music was going on in your household when you were young, and can you recall something that made a distinct impression on you back then?

Okay well yeah, in my household my father is a musician. He was a saxophone player. His brother, my uncle, was a drummer. And my other uncle was an arranger and a piano player and he played tuba. And my father had the Italian feast bands where they, you know, they always pin the money on the thing. And so I started playing with that little band when I was like eight and I was playing drums then. And my mother thought the drums were a little bit noisy and, much to her chagrin, I ended up with the trumpet which is as bad as the drums as far as she was concerned. So yeah I had a lot of influence, family influence.
